grh_27c482da5eb845bb8d50.title: The Ghost Breakers
paragraphs: Radio crime-buster Larry Lawrence is hired by Mary Carter, who has inherited Black Island off Cuba and the ominous Castillo Maldito. The castle is reputed to be haunted, but Larry follows Mary to the island despite gangsters, warnings, and a very convincing zombie. Inside the castle the pair discover that the supernatural effects are being manufactured to frighten Mary away from a valuable mine on the property. Montgomery and his confederates are behind the ghostly tricks, while Frenchy Duvall closes in from another direction. The rival villains finally shoot each other, the police take control, and Mary keeps the mine. Larry leaves Cuba rich enough to joke about financing her television career, still insisting there are no such things as ghosts even after everything they have seen.

[[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Bob Hope, Shirley Mitchell, Sheldon Leonard, and Howard Wiley. Other credited names include Richard Allen Simmons as radio adaptor and Jimmy Wallington as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.50075df24f7e1a61|Anacin]] and [[org|org.f431bbef0d9d6a89|RCA Victor (Chesterfield commercial deleted)]].
This version presents a radio version of [[work|work.sdp.film.75df7601ace10c97|The Ghost Breakers]]. Richard Allen Simmons adapted it for radio.

grh_27046facaac83c5773b9.title: The Speckled Band
paragraphs: Helen Stoner fears she will die as her sister did after hearing strange nighttime music in a bedroom with a dummy bell rope, a ventilator into Dr. Roylott's room and a bed fixed to the floor. Holmes and Watson keep watch and see a venomous snake crawl through the ventilator and down the rope toward the bed. Holmes strikes it with his cane, sending it back through the opening, where it bites Roylott instead; the 'speckled band' is revealed as the snake Roylott trained with a whistle to murder his stepdaughters.

paragraphs: Young Frederick believes his apprenticeship to a comic band of pirates ends when he turns twenty-one, freeing him to leave them and marry Mabel.
